| | Answer | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| a | consumer, 306,611,606원 | 2nd smb 259,696,752 · 3rd enterprise 241,057,459 |
| b | 248 customers | Counted by unique email |
| c | hw, 285,961,621원 | 2nd svc 284,825,108, about 1.1M behind |
| d | 2025-06 | 314,277,392원 |
| e | u246@ex.com | Refunds 2,218,000원, no tie |
| f | 230 customers | Counted by unique email |
| g | 669,457원 | 1,206 paid Q3 orders |
| h | 9.6% | August 258,240,287 → September 283,056,559 (9.6098%) |

**How the data was handled:**
- **Time zone:** I added 9 hours to the UTC times before deciding dates. 87 paid orders sit within 9 hours of the Q3 start or end in UTC, so this changes which orders count as Q3.
- **Segments:** There are 6 raw values with different spacing and capitals, which combine into 3 segments. Categories needed no cleanup.
- **Duplicate accounts:** 300 accounts share 250 emails. Questions b, e and f count by email.
- **Data checks:** Only one table field needed cleaning (segment). Refunds always match an item on the order and never exceed the quantity bought. Every order points to an existing customer and product.

**Decision for you:** 40 of the people with duplicate accounts have different segments on their different accounts. For (a), I used the segment of the account that placed each order. Consumer leads by about 47M, so I expect another way of assigning segments to give the same winner. I didn't re-run the numbers to confirm that.
